articles.description:
I vendored an audio deepfake detector into my verification platform. It loaded cleanly, every integration check passed, and the forward pass looked healthy. Then I measured it on a held-out slice and got an AUC of 0.54 — barely above chance. The vendor reports 0.9967. This is the story of what happened in between, and why I decided not to ship it.
The model is Spectra-AASIST3, an audio deepfake detector released under Apache-2.0. I vendored it into the project as a potential audio channel for a WhatsApp-first deepfake and malware verification platform. The integration work was straightforward and, by every check I ran, successful.
The checkpoint loaded without a single mismatch: 1022 out of 1022 keys matched and applied, 318.9 million parameters. The forward pass was responsive and produce…
articles.title: I rejected a model that passed everyone else's benchmark

articles.description:
Hi everyone,
I built a free print scale checker as part of my printer test site, after running into a frustrating problem: prints that look fine but come out the wrong size.
The usual cause: an A4 file printed on Letter with "Fit to page" on shrinks to about 94%. Nothing looks broken, but templates, labels and patterns are off.
What I focused on:
Print one sheet, measure a 100 mm bar, type the number
It tells you the scale and whether it matches a paper-size mismatch
Runs in the browser, nothing uploaded
What I learned:
"The printer printed" and "it printed correctly" are different checks
Real vector PDFs beat HTML print for exact sizes
Question for developers: have you built anything that has to print at an exact size? How did you test it?
articles.title: I built a tiny tool that catches the "printed at 94%" problem

WebAssembly allows applications written in languages other than JavaScript to execute directly in the browser. With WebForms Core 2.2, Java can also be used as a WebAssembly Commander and generate WebForms commands that are executed by WebFormsJS.
For Java, WebForms Core currently supports TeaVM as its supported WebAssembly compiler.
The architecture is straightforward:
Java
 ↓
TeaVM
 ↓
WebAssembly
 ↓
WebForms Core
 ↓
WebFormsJS
 ↓
HTML DOM

The important point is that Java does not manipulate the browser DOM directly. The Java code generates a WebForms response, and WebFormsJS executes that response in the browser.
TeaVM compiles Java bytecode to WebAssembly. WebForms Core can use the resulting WebAssembly module as a Commander.

articles.author: jasonmills94
articles.description:
Email fixtures are easy to add to a CI pipeline and surprisingly hard to retire. A test creates a disposable inbox, starts a Kubernetes Job, waits for a verification message, and then the pipeline moves on. If the runner is canceled, the namespace is deleted half way, or the worker loses its lease, the fixture can stay around longer than the test that created it.
That is not just wasted cluster capacity. Old inboxes and test payloads can expose data to later runs, while orphaned Jobs make a busy EKS cluster harder to operate. The pattern that worked for me is simple: every run gets one bounded identity, one cleanup owner, and one receipt that proves what happened.
Teams often treat cleanup as a final shell step:
kubectl delete job email-check-$RUN_ID -n $NAMESPACE

This works until the she…
articles.title: Kubernetes Email Jobs Need a Cleanup Owner

A small open call, and a small experiment.
I built an open-source tool for my partner that reads a NinjaTrader trade export and tells her what her own history says: which New York session made her money, what her first five trades of the day cost her, and what re-entering within 15 minutes of a loss cost her. On her account those three were +$1,167 vs +$8 by session, -$327 vs +$2,160 by trade-of-day, and -$179 vs +$1,396 by re-entry timing. She had felt all three and known none of the numbers.
I'd like to know how typical that is, and the only way to find out is more accounts. So:
The offer. Email a month (or more) of your trade export to aipossiblee@gmail.com with the subject "Three numbers". NinjaTrader 8's Trade Performance export is native; any broker CSV with one row per trade works. …
